expectations.text: Uses cdkTrapFocus or CdkTrapFocus directive from @angular/cdk/a11y for focus trapping
expectations.evidence: The dialog template applies `cdkTrapFocus` and `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture="true"` to the inner card div, and `A11yModule` is imported from `@angular/cdk/a11y`. The design-decisions section also explicitly explains why cdkTrapFocus was chosen over a manual Tab keydown handler.

expectations.text: Dialog has role='dialog' and aria-modal='true' or uses the native <dialog> element
expectations.evidence: The component's `host` object contains `role: 'dialog'` and `'aria-modal': 'true'` (transcript lines 94-95), setting both attributes statically on the host element.

expectations.text: Focus moves to the dialog on open (autoFocus or programmatic focus)
expectations.evidence: `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture="true"` causes CDK to move focus into the trap region when it is activated. The Cancel button carries `cdkFocusInitial`, making it the specific first-focus target. Documented in the accessibility checklist: 'cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture="true" + cdkFocusInitial on Cancel button'.

expectations.text: Escape key closes the dialog via keyboard event handler
expectations.evidence: The `host` object contains `'(keydown.escape)': 'handleEscape($event)'`. The `handleEscape` method calls `event.preventDefault()`, `event.stopPropagation()`, and `this.closeDialog.emit('cancelled')`, which triggers teardown in the service.

expectations.text: Focus returns to the trigger element after dialog closes
expectations.evidence: In `confirmation-dialog.service.ts` (FINAL version), `const triggerElement = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null` is captured before opening. Inside the `closeDialog` subscription, `restoreFocus(triggerElement)` is called after `componentRef.destroy()`. The `restoreFocus` helper calls `target.focus()` if the element is still in the document, falling back to `document.body.focus()`.

expectations.text: Background content uses the inert attribute or aria-hidden='true'
expectations.evidence: The service snapshots all existing `<body>` children into `bodyChildren` before appending the dialog host, then calls `child.setAttribute('inert', '')` on each. On close, `child.removeAttribute('inert')` restores them. The transcript explicitly explains why `inert` is preferred over `aria-hidden`.
`changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` is set in the `@Component` decorator of `ConfirmationDialogComponent` (transcript line 91). It is also set on the `UsageExampleComponent` consumer.

expectations.text: Has aria-labelledby or aria-label for the dialog title
expectations.evidence: The `host` object contains `'[attr.aria-labelledby]': '"confirmation-dialog-title"'` (transcript line 98), bound to `<h2 id="confirmation-dialog-title">` in the template. `aria-describedby` pointing to the message paragraph is also present as a bonus.

claims.claim: Tested interaction flow with NVDA + Chrome and VoiceOver + Safari
claims.evidence: The transcript asserts screen reader testing was done, but the output is a code-only transcript with no test run artifacts, browser logs, or CI results. This cannot be verified from the available outputs.

claims.claim: White text on red (#dc2626) achieves 5.0:1 contrast ratio
claims.evidence: The WCAG contrast ratio for white (#ffffff) on #dc2626 is approximately 5.0:1, which meets WCAG AA for normal text (4.5:1 required). This can be independently verified.

All 8 graded expectations pass, and the accessibility checklist in the transcript accounts for each WAI-ARIA pattern requirement (focus trap, escape, focus restore, inert background, ARIA roles and labels).

claims.claim: The first teardown implementation in the service has a bug (appRef.detachView called with no argument)
claims.evidence: The first `ConfirmationDialogService` snippet shows `this.appRef.detachView(` with an inline comment admitting the problem; the transcript then supplies a corrected FINAL version that replaces it with `componentRef.destroy()`. The final version is complete and correct.

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks that the `inert` attribute is removed from background siblings after the dialog closes. An implementation that applies `inert` but never removes it would pass the current assertion and leave the app permanently broken after first use.

suggestions.assertion: Focus returns to the trigger element after dialog closes
suggestions.reason: The assertion would also pass if focus is restored to `document.body` (the fallback in `restoreFocus`). Consider tightening to verify that focus returns specifically to the element that opened the dialog, not just any element.

No assertion checks that the CDK focus trap is properly cleaned up (destroyed/deactivated) when the dialog is removed from the DOM. `cdkTrapFocus` holds listeners; failing to destroy the component correctly would leak them. The implementation handles this via `componentRef.destroy()`, but no eval verifies it.

eval_feedback.overall: The evals cover all eight core accessibility requirements and the implementation satisfies all of them with high quality. The three suggestions above address post-close cleanup and specificity gaps that could allow subtly broken implementations to pass.
